races.name: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Out-and-out hold-up horse whose recent form shows a win and place at 6f on good, but drops back to 5f here and has not won or placed in similar going at this trip — trainer Jack Jones in modest 14-day form (2/14), and the step down in distance is a genuine concern for a horse who needs time to wind up.
runners_data.comment: Wyle Cop was fifth last time out but has a third two starts back, and another third six starts back among his recent efforts; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. He remains without a win in that spell, the obvious catch.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Strong recent form on good ground — placed or won in three of last four at 6f good — but this is 5f and her natural style is hold-up, meaning she is pushed towards midfield rather than her true rearward position; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps the weight, and she remains a live contender if she can find the gaps on a flat straight track.
runners_data.comment: Come On Over won last time out and was runner-up two starts back, form that makes him one to respect; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. The concern is the mixed efforts further back, including an eighth and an unplaced run.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the race's pace-maker; John Wainwright's sole runner in a 1/1 trainer 14-day snippet suggests confidence, and she has placed twice at 5f good, but STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects the risk that her lead role may expose her when a big field of closers descend late.
runners_data.comment: Startling is an outsider on our figures despite a pair of seconds last time out and two starts back, and she has also raced over today's trip and going before. She remains without a win in this spell, though, with a pulled-up effort among her recent starts.

runners_data.name: Papa Don't Preach
runners_data.note: A veteran seven-year-old who is a genuine hold-up type, wearing hood (hg:h), with his best form on standown and good ground at 5f — placed three times in five recent runs at this trip — but 70 days off the track is a significant flag and his true style is obscured by being redistributed into midfield on the map.
runners_data.comment: Papa Don't Preach was well beaten in ninth last time out and remains winless in his last six starts, though a string of thirds and fifths make up the rest of that form. A 70-day layoff since that run counts against him, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: The only non-redistributed hold-up runner, J Street won at 5f on Southwell (standown) and has placed at this trip on good; Lewis Chalkley's 5lb claim is useful, and his style and course-distance suitability make him one of the most naturally suited runners to the race shape as it shapes up.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and fourth last time out, J Street has the leading rating here and has also raced over today's trip and going before; the risk is the fifth- and sixth-placed efforts either side that show she can find one below her best.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Won his last start at 6f on good (OR progression), carries a hood (hg:t) and is trained by Harry Eustace who is in solid 14-day form (3/14); a true hold-up type repositioned to midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers, but nine-from-fifteen similar-going record and course knowledge at age eight are worth noting alongside his STYLE_FIT discount.
runners_data.comment: Ancient Times won last time out and returns quickly nine days on, form that has him rated among the leading contenders here; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. The one blot is the three well-beaten efforts that came before that win.

races.paceDynamic: Startling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner sprint and, with no genuine rivals to press her from the gates, she is expected to dictate an honest but uncontested tempo over the straight five furlongs on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster. The pack behind her is dominated by hold-up horses — Wyle Cop, J Street, Come On Over, Papa Don't Preach and Ancient Times all prefer to race off the pace — meaning Startling will control the fractions without being harassed, setting up a race shape where the key question is whether her lead is sustainable or catchable. This shape structurally favours hold-up types coming from off the pace in the final two furlongs, but with so many closers chasing the same late ground, the winner will need to be the sharpest finisher who finds the cleanest route. Three runners — Come On Over, Papa Don't Preach and Ancient Times — are true hold-up types mapped to midfield purely because the field is saturated with closers; Ancient Times (won at this trip on good), Come On Over (strong recent form on good ground at 6f), and J Street (the one hold-up runner not redistributed) are best positioned to exploit the pace shape, with hold-up and late-running profiles the clear beneficiaries of Startling's lone-leader scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Startling Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Startling leads at a fair but uncontested pace and the hold-up pack arrives in the final furlong with a clean run.
scenarios.body: Startling sets the fractions alone but the effort of leading six furlongs of hard ground means she is vulnerable inside the final furlong; the sharpest finisher from the chasing pack collects as she ties up. J Street and Come On Over, both with strong form on good ground at sprint trips, are best placed to pounce with a late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Startling Steals It Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Startling jumps cleanly, builds an early lead and the pace she sets is simply too slow to set up a winning late run.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the front end, Startling controls the race entirely to her own rhythm and has enough in reserve to hold on through the final furlong; at OR 61 she is well-treated if allowed to bowl along unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congested Finish, One Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of closers get baulked or traffic issues arise in the straight and one runner finds daylight earlier than the rest.
scenarios.body: With five hold-up types all hunting the same ground late, gaps will be at a premium; any runner who secures a clean early passage wide or on the rail gains a crucial advantage over those stuck in traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Out-of-Role Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types — forced to race closer to the pace than ideal — unexpectedly benefits from a position nearer Startling.
scenarios.body: If Come On Over or Papa Don't Preach happen to slot into a prominent berth and the pace slackens, they could sit a length off Startling and pounce before the true closers can wind up; both carry STYLE_FIT discounts making this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: J Street has the cleanest profile for the race shape — hold-up type, 5f good-ground form, non-redistributed — watch for him getting a clear run down the Doncaster straight from the two-furlong pole.

Ancient Times won last time on good going and Eustace is hitting form (3/14); watch whether Travis Ford (7lb claim) can navigate through the congested late-running pack, as he could be the value in the hold-up group.

Startling's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — if she is allowed to dictate a slow early tempo the closers may not reel her in; watch the opening splits carefully to judge whether the pace is truly sustainable.

Come On Over is a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield on the map — Whiteley must decide early whether to push forward or drop back to her natural position; a confused tactical ride is the key risk for what is otherwise a form-fit runner.

With five closers all seeking the same ground in the final furlong, traffic incidents on the straight course are a real possibility — any runner drawn wide may have an advantage in finding clean air without being hemmed in.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier)
Lakeside Village Is 30 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner for Edward Bethell with Kevin Stott up; holds its most recent Good-ground form at this exact trip although the recent form string of 469-09 offers no encouragement, and a style-fit flag means the race is unlikely to play to its strengths if pressure materialises.
runners_data.comment: A rating of 97 (second of nine) puts him right into this, with the stable firing at a 26% strike rate in the last fortnight. Yet to win in five starts and finishes have been modest of late, so turning talent into a result is the query.

runners_data.name: Kodi Lion
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's five-year-old returns after 267 days off — the lengthy absence is the headline concern — but has placed at 7f on Good ground twice in his career and Rawlinson knows the horse well; fitness will be the arbiter.
runners_data.comment: A rating of 96 (third of nine) keeps him well involved on quality, and a good second four starts back shows the engine is there. Yet to win in five starts, and a 267-day absence plus a cold stable (4% last fortnight) is the serious query.

runners_data.name: Akkadian Thunder
runners_data.note: David O'Meara sends this hold-up type out 14 days after its last start, which counts as a quick turnaround but the horse has been running consistently; three of its last five came at 7f on Good ground, and David Nolan's low-key style suits waiting tactics.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, but a rating of 98 — the highest in the field — marks him the one to beat on figures, with a good third three starts back showing more to come. Quick back inside a fortnight, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old wears a hood and steps back to 7f after a run of 8f starts — the trip shortening is a live positive angle; Kieran O'Neill keeps the ride, and three top-four finishes from recent Good/Soft ground runs at middle distances suggest the extra speed emphasis suits.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, and a rating of 89 (seventh of nine) — level with his official mark — offers little upside. A third three starts back is the pick of a mixed sequence otherwise blighted by an unplaced run and a ninth.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's four-year-old wears a hood and showed a sharp second over 8f on Good ground last time; Ben Robinson takes the ride and the horse's hold-up style means it needs the pace to collapse late, which the current race shape makes far from certain.
runners_data.comment: A below-par unplaced run last time out is a blot after a good second two starts back, leaving a mixed impression. A rating of 91 (fifth of nine) rates her a fair each-way sort, and she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Talis Evolvere
runners_data.note: Hannon's six-year-old has a strong prominent racing instinct but the field is crowded with pace types and it has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map; its best recent form (2nd, Soft, 8f) came at a longer trip, and on fast going over 7f its sim-going record of 3/15 is poor.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts, and a rating of 89 (eighth of nine) leaves plenty to find on figures. Two runner-up efforts in the mix show there's ability, but three modest finishes further back temper any optimism.

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old steps up sharply from six furlongs to seven — every one of its last five starts has been at 6f, making the extra furlong untested territory; sim-going form is solid (8/9) but Rhys Clutterbuck's claim and the trip extension are both unknowns.
runners_data.comment: A standout speed figure of 95 and a hot yard — 31% in the last fortnight — support a rating of 94 (fourth of nine). Yet to win in five starts, though, with a below-par ninth two starts back the main concern.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has run all five recent starts on Good ground at Doncaster's home trip or thereabouts, giving Fentiman clear course-and-distance pattern to work from; a recent second over 7f here is the most relevant piece of form in the race.
runners_data.comment: A good second four starts back is the highlight of an otherwise modest sequence that includes an unplaced effort and a ninth. A rating of 90 (sixth of nine) is a fair reflection, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old is naturally a prominent-to-front-running type, but the overcrowded pace cloth means it is likely to find itself racing in unfamiliar midfield territory; its win and placed efforts came when able to secure a forward berth, so the style-fit discount is meaningful.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of the pile on a rating of 86 (ninth of nine), though a fair third last time out and a win five starts back show there's some ability there. He faces a tough task on these figures, but has raced over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Yorkshire is the lone confirmed front runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster's flat seven furlongs, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any genuine pressure forcing the pace up. Behind Yorkshire, Christian David and Daydreama are the natural prominent chasers, with Kodi Lion also capable of racing close to the speed, meaning a small group will track the leader without any combustive head-to-head battle developing. This field does hold more prominent-minded types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — First Time and Talis Evolvere are genuine front-to-prominent and hold-up horses respectively who are likely to find themselves squeezed into a midfield berth against their natural instincts. The resulting shape — one uncontested leader, a bunched chasing pack, and a modest tempo on fast ground over seven furlongs — classically favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort to the line, rather than deep closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Yorkshire dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop and the prominent chasers track without drama, setting up a straight-line stamina test.
scenarios.body: Yorkshire's uncontested lead produces a well-strung-out finish where those racing in the first four lengths dominate the closing stages; Christian David and Daydreama, both comfortable prominent types on Good to Firm ground, are ideally placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively quick early and the prominent horses tie up, allowing the genuine midfielders to reel them in.
scenarios.body: A brisk early tempo would stretch the field and leave a gap for Akkadian Thunder or Perfect Part to pick their way through late; both are honest hold-up types with recent good-ground form who would welcome any cut in the leaders' stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Yorkshire is allowed to dictate an almost walk-and-sprint pace and simply outstays rivals who never get into a rhythm.
scenarios.body: On fast ground over Doncaster's straight seven, a horse that has controlled every yard can punch clear in the final furlong before closers close the gap; Yorkshire's style fit here is genuine and a slow, dawdling pace plays entirely to its strength.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the race burns off the prominent horses, leaving the rear-guard to finish fastest.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends partly on Talis Evolvere and Egoli, neither of whom has compelling evidence they can close from off a hot gallop over this trip on fast ground; the low probability reflects both the lack of a true pace battle and the style-fit concerns flagged for the redistributed types.

watchPoints.text: Daydreama has the strongest course-and-distance profile in the race — watch whether Fentiman can slot in second or third off Yorkshire's lead, as that position makes it the horse most likely to sustain the run through the final two furlongs.

Kodi Lion's 267-day absence is the single biggest fitness risk flag in the race; if Rawlinson is forced to chase the pace early on its comeback run, the hold-up tendencies from its pre-layoff form suggest it could empty in the final furlong.

First Time is a genuine front-runner being squeezed into midfield by an overcrowded pace cloth — watch whether McHugh pushes up to claim a prominent berth regardless, which could inject an unexpected injection of early pace and unsettle Yorkshire's rhythm.

Egoli has never raced beyond 6f — watch its early movement for signs of travelling comfortably at the longer trip, as Ralph Beckett's runners often show improvement second time stepping up in distance but the first attempt carries inherent uncertainty.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race after earlier-card updates; horses with strong sim-going records on similar fast surfaces (Yorkshire, Daydreama, Egoli) carry a small but genuine edge over those whose best form has come on Soft.

races.name: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, rated OR 64 and in winning form at seven furlongs on Good (1/7f/GOO in recent history), but jockey William Pyle's trainer is winless in 14 days (0/4) and Travis is technically a prominent horse leading — a slight style stretch that could catch up if pressed harder than expected.
runners_data.comment: Travis won two starts back and was only beaten into third last time out, a much-improved sequence after a blank spell in between; he has also raced over today's distance and going before. The one blot is the pair of unplaced efforts further back in that run.

runners_data.name: Thapa VC
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott takes over on this eight-year-old handicapper who has hit the frame multiple times at 7-8f on Good, and while his tongue-tie is noted, his true hold-up style means he needs a meaningful gallop to deliver his finishing kick — the single controlled pace-setter here is a concern for his chances.
runners_data.comment: Thapa VC was second two starts back and has been placed three times in his last six starts, form that puts him firmly in this on our figures; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. He remains without a win in that spell, though, the obvious catch.

runners_data.name: Maxi Boy
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old course-compatible hold-up performer who placed at 7f on Good (4/7f/GOO) but whose trainer McSharry is 0/2 in the last fortnight; the short sprint trip over six furlongs that features heavily in his history suggests seven furlongs is his absolute limit rather than his sweet spot.
runners_data.comment: Maxi Boy tops our figures in this field but is yet to turn that into a big finish, fourth last time out and fourth again three starts back. He has also raced over today's trip and going before, though he remains without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Renewable Dream
runners_data.note: Absent 173 days — the longest layoff in this field — and a genuine hold-up horse whose last two runs on Good ground yielded thirds at 8f, though stepping back to 7f and running fresh off that break introduces real unknowns; his true position at the rear of the field will not be served by a modest pace.
runners_data.comment: Renewable Dream was well beaten in ninth last time out, some way below the pair of thirds he showed earlier in this run, and he remains winless in his last five starts. A 173-day absence since that run is the further complication, though he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: War And Love
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's yard is in decent nick (2/13 in 14 days) and War And Love placed at 8f on Good recently, but this horse's authentic hold-up style means he will be last or second-last away and a soft pace set by Travis makes his finishing effort harder to land; trip down to 7f is a marginal positive.
runners_data.comment: War And Love is a rank outsider on our figures, though her recent form has some substance: third last time out, and a second four starts back among the runs in between. She has run over today's distance before, but remains without a win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Wilde And Dandy
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's string has been busy (2/28 in 14 days) and Wilde And Dandy has placed at 7f on Good (3/7f/GOO), but as a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on the pace map to midfield, he will realistically be held up late — Stevie Donohoe would need to be very proactive from the stalls for this to change.
runners_data.comment: Wilde And Dandy was third last time out, matching a similar effort four starts back, and carries a fair speed figure into this; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. The risk is the pair of much worse efforts in between, a ninth and a sixth.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Connected to a yard (Easterby) with 2/28 in 14 days and has placed four times at 6f on Good, but the step up to 7f is genuinely untested territory for a horse whose entire recent profile is built over sprint distances; apprentice Lewis Chalkley (7lb claim) is an advantage on the weights but he is a true hold-up type forced further forward on the map only by the volume of rear-runners.
runners_data.comment: Big Apple Jack was runner-up last time out, and second again four starts back, form that shows he can be competitive in this grade; he has also raced over today's trip and going before. An eighth and an unplaced effort either side temper the case, and he remains without a win in this spell.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: Wearing a hood and with a remarkable 13/15 similar-going record, this OR-56 mare has finished second an extraordinary five times recently at 7f on Good — she knows how to travel prominently and sustain her effort; with Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) in the saddle and a genuine prominent style, she is structurally the best-placed horse to benefit from this controlled pace.
runners_data.comment: Havana Mojito has been second in each of his last three starts, a notably consistent frame effort that hasn't yet translated into a win in his last five starts. He has also raced over today's trip and going before, though he is only the seventh of eight on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and a true hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map does not reflect how Faye McManoman is likely to deploy him; Nigel Tinkler's yard is productive (3/20 in 14 days) but a second at 7f on Soft is his best recent effort and the drop back from 8f might not fully compensate for his well-documented tendency to weaken when asked for a final effort.

races.paceDynamic: Travis is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Havana Mojito as the only other prominent-style runner, these two will set a controlled, measured tempo over Doncaster's straight seven furlongs on going that is effectively Good To Firm — fast enough to reward those who travel well but not so extreme as to destroy the pace. With just two horses likely to push forward, the gallop will be sustainable rather than searching, meaning Travis can dictate without being harassed and Havana Mojito can slot in behind without burning petrol. The bulk of this field — Thapa VC, Maxi Boy, War And Love and Sir David — are genuine hold-up types who will need the pace to collapse, which a lone, unchallenged front-runner on fast ground makes less certain. Renewable Dream, Wilde And Dandy and Big Apple Jack are true hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield mapping because there are simply too many rear-end runners for the race shape to accommodate naturally — of that group, Wilde And Dandy and Big Apple Jack are most likely to at least secure a handy midfield berth in practice. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Travis without expending energy, as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough for the true closers to peel off the back of the field and pick up winners late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Front Two Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Travis leads uncontested at a fair clip with Havana Mojito tracking close and neither is seriously challenged for position.
scenarios.body: Travis dictates a controlled gallop and Havana Mojito, with an excellent record of placing on Good ground at seven furlongs, is ideally placed to pick up the pieces if Travis fades; the sustainable tempo plays to both prominent runners' strengths while leaving closers with too little to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Lucky Splits
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is just honest enough to string out the field and a well-positioned hold-up horse finds a gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Thapa VC or War And Love, travelling through the race from a midfield position, could time a late run to exploit any tiring front-runners; this scenario needs the pace to be a touch quicker than expected, which is plausible but not favoured given just one genuine pace-setter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Travis goes too hard early or the field dawdles chaotically and the pace completely falls apart in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Maxi Boy or Thapa VC, genuine hold-up horses on a course and distance that suits them, could overhaul a weakening Travis if the early fractions were deceptive; however, a lone front-runner on fast ground rarely blows up in this fashion, making this the least structurally likely outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horse Grabs Spot
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses remapped to midfield actually secures a prominent early position and controls the race from the front rank.
scenarios.body: Wilde And Dandy or Big Apple Jack, if hustled forward by their jockeys against their natural grain, could find an uncontested prominent berth and run a career-best from the front; their STYLE_FIT discounts make this structurally unlikely and their form when not getting their natural run is not encouraging.

watchPoints.text: Havana Mojito — if she tracks Travis smoothly in second with Whiteley patient, she has the profile (prominent, multiple 2nds on Good at 7f, hood, form:45222) to dictate the finish if Travis fades; watch whether Whiteley settles her immediately or gets into a duel.

Travis — as the sole pace-setter, the tempo he sets is the single biggest lever in this race; if he goes leisurely, front-runners dominate and closers are cooked, but any early pressure from jockeys eager to get their hold-up horses moving could see him quicken and then collapse in the final furlong.

Renewable Dream — 173 days off and a true hold-up horse needing a strong gallop that this race is not set to provide; watch the market move pre-race, as any significant support off that layoff with trainer T14 form of 1/1 could signal stable confidence worth noting.

Thapa VC and War And Love — both genuine hold-up horses with Kevin Stott and Ben Robinson respectively; watch whether either jockey breaks with their horse's natural style and pushes forward early, as any change of approach from these experienced riders would shift the tactical picture materially.

Big Apple Jack — the step up from 6f to 7f is an uncharted question for this horse; watch the opening furlong to see whether Chalkley rides him aggressively to find that midfield slot the pace map suggests, or whether he settles in his natural hold-up position and concedes ground before the race begins in earnest.

races.name: Summer Saturdays At Doncaster Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Ed Dunlop with Sam James aboard, returning after 45 days off; all four runs on similar going have produced zero wins and zero places, and the step up to 1m4f at Doncaster doesn't obviously unlock improvement — likely to be outpaced from the rear in a controlled tempo race.
runners_data.comment: That Darn Cantor is the outsider of this race on our figures, some way below his official mark after a run of sixth, fifth, ninth and seventh in his last four starts with no finish inside the frame. He has raced over today's going before, though a lengthy absence since that run counts further against him.

runners_data.name: Rossa Raheen
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners this Ollie Sangster three-year-old who is a true hold-up type by nature; despite the map showing a midfield slot, it will in practice race from the rear and faces a tactical disadvantage if Tai Hang Pegasus sets only a gentle pace — one win and one place from six runs on comparable ground suggests ability exists if conditions click.
runners_data.comment: Rossa Raheen was fourth last time out, and was runner-up three starts back, form that keeps her firmly involved on our figures; she has also raced over today's going before. The blot is the unplaced effort four starts back, and she remains without a win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has a pair of second-place finishes over 10f in recent starts and looks the most credentialed of the hold-up brigade for this trip; apprentice Seamus Cronin (5lb claim) is a meaningful weight advantage, and the step to 1m4f on Good to Firm at a flat track aligns well with its distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Royal Poetry was runner-up last time out, and won four starts back, with another second three starts back underlining her consistency at this level; she has also raced over today's going before. The main query is the 39-day gap since that run, following a below-par seventh two starts back.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter, Charlie Fellowes's runner has course-and-distance form (2nd over 12f, Good) and Stevie Donohoe should be able to dictate on a flat track with no rivals likely to contest the lead; however, the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 and a recent form string of 4762 temper enthusiasm about whether it can win from the front rather than merely setting the table.
runners_data.comment: Tai Hang Pegasus was runner-up last time out and is quick to reappear nine days on, form that puts him right among the leading contenders on our figures. He has also raced over today's trip and going before, though he remains without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Willow Wood
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's runner won over 12f on Soft last time out and represents the most compelling prominent-tracking profile in the field; George Downing rides and the return to Good to Firm is a going unknown for the trip, but the ability to sit close to Tai Hang Pegasus and unleash a turn-of-foot in the straight makes this horse the most naturally suited to the anticipated race shape.
runners_data.comment: Willow Wood won last time out, but that came 44 days ago and the form before it was modest, no better than fourth in the four starts prior. She has run over today's distance before, though the lengthy absence and moderate depth of that form make her hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Boilermaker
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 66) carries first-time headgear and is a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map by the surplus of rear-runners; two placed efforts over 12f on Good ground show stamina is not in doubt, but Lewis Edmunds faces an uphill task if the pace is insufficient to set up a late run from the back.
runners_data.comment: Boilermaker was third last time out, having been runner-up two starts back, continuing a clear upward trend after a fourth and a pair of sevenths further back. He has also raced over today's trip and going before, and the one small concern is that he is still without a win in this spell.

races.paceDynamic: Tai Hang Pegasus is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Stevie Donohoe can dictate a measured, energy-conserving gallop from the front. Willow Wood is the one prominent type who may track closely, but the pace is unlikely to be pressured into anything taxing — this is a race where the tempo will be controlled and sustainable throughout. Rossa Raheen and Boilermaker are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map purely because the field holds more rear-of-field types than there are positions for; in practice they will race further back than their mapped slot suggests, meaning the true closer contingent is larger than it appears. This race shape — a lone leader setting a fair but uncontested gallop on fast ground over a staying trip — classically favours prominent racers or hold-up horses with a strong late kick, provided there is sufficient pace to aim at, which Tai Hang Pegasus alone may or may not generate at a level that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Late Drive
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus controls a comfortable, unhurried pace and the field bunches behind, setting up a straight-line sprint for home.
scenarios.body: Tai Hang Pegasus dictates throughout at a controlled tempo on the Good to Firm ground, with Willow Wood tracking close enough to pounce; the lack of pace pressure means those with a strong finishing kick through the final two furlongs are best placed. Royal Poetry and Willow Wood, both proven over 10f and with form in similar conditions, are ideally suited to this shape where a steady run-and-sprint scenario rewards those travelling well into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Rolls Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus is allowed to steal an uncontested advantage and the hold-up brigade fails to close from their true rear positions.
scenarios.body: With no genuine front-runner to push Tai Hang Pegasus, Donohoe could manufacture a winning lead by gradually lengthening stride from two furlongs out while the true closers — Rossa Raheen and Boilermaker — are slow to recognise the move from the back. Tai Hang Pegasus's recent course form (2nd over 12f, Good) and the STYLE_FIT caveat are partially offset by the luxury of an uncontested lead on fast ground at a flat, galloping track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus goes too slow, the field coils up and a strong late surge rewards the truest hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: A crawl early would compress the field and theoretically benefit the hold-up types, but both Rossa Raheen and Boilermaker are redistributed — they are genuine closers who will sit last rather than midfield, meaning they face the hardest ask if the pace is insufficient to string the field out. Royal Poetry's two recent second-place efforts over 10f in similar going give it the best realistic claim among the hold-up contingent if a finishing burst materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus fades dramatically in the straight after over-exerting early, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but non-zero possibility given Tai Hang Pegasus's recent form string of 6-4762 and the STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it is racing out of its natural role; if it overcooks the pace relative to what the field expects and then weakens, Willow Wood — who was prominent last time out when winning over 12f on Soft — could capitalise having tracked throughout. That Darn Cantor and Boilermaker are each too far back in this shape to benefit meaningfully.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Willow Wood travels close enough to Tai Hang Pegasus in the early stages — if George Downing tracks the leader from the second furlong, Willow Wood becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given its recent 12f win and proximity to the pace.

Tai Hang Pegasus's true running style is Prominent rather than a dominant front-runner — if Donohoe is passive early, another horse could accidentally assume the lead and the anticipated pace scenario collapses entirely.

Rossa Raheen and Boilermaker are both genuine closers who will race further back than their midfield map positions; if Tai Hang Pegasus sets a crawl, these two are unlikely to generate enough momentum from the rear to pounce in time on a flat track.

Royal Poetry's apprentice claim of 5lb for Seamus Cronin is a tangible weight relief in a field where every pound matters at 1m4f in a handicap — watch for it travelling powerfully on the outside approaching the straight if the pace is genuinely fair.

The going has been reported as Good to Firm for this race throughout the card despite the headline suggesting Good — all runners show an OK going flag, but horses with Soft-ground form flags (Rossa Raheen, Willow Wood) should be monitored in the paddock for market moves that reflect connections' confidence on the faster surface.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over this course-and-distance in his most recent outing 14 days ago — strong going form and trip form tick but six-runner handicap form needs replicating in this 11-runner field where clear passage from the rear is less guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a run of modest efforts and returns quickly here, just 14 days later. Has raced over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 66 (third of 11) keeps him well involved without being the pick on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Penny Ghent
runners_data.note: Dual course-and-distance winner with a genuine come-from-behind style and a blinkered headgear flag; 49 days off the track is a slight concern but Simon Whitaker's 1/1 T14 record and sharp recent form string (-90113) suggests she returns ready.
runners_data.comment: A pair of wins two and three starts back followed two well-beaten efforts, and she rounded off with a fair third last time out — a progressive spell. A rating of 56 (tenth of 11) and a 49-day absence still leave her among the hardest to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Clasina
runners_data.note: Strong recent form includes two placings at 7f on similar ground, but her true instinct is to race from the rear — mapped to midfield here simply because the field is overcrowded with hold-up types, and in practice she may find herself behind more horses than ideal with limited ground to make up.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and was placed in the two runs before that, with a rating of 65 (fourth of 11) keeping her firmly involved. The blot is a below-par run last time out, though she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning in her last six, racing prominently to hold-up hybrid style over this trip and going; Alan Brown's 0/10 T14 record is a damaging angle, and while she hits the frame regularly her win conversion at this level is poor.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts but the form reads well, and a rating of 68 (second of 11) puts her right amongst the leading contenders. Quick to reappear just nine days on, and she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and the key pace-shaper; her record on good ground and at this trip is thin (0W1P in 3 similar-going runs) and her style fit tag suggests she may race further forward than her natural comfort zone, yet her tactical advantage here is substantial.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts, though a good second two starts back shows ability, even if last time's sixth fits a mixed pattern. A rating of 63 (sixth of 11) makes him a fair midfield type who has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Progressive five-year-old with back-to-back wins including over 10f on good ground; Kevin Stott takes over in the saddle and the prominent racing style fits this pace map perfectly — likely to sit a length or two off Relevant Range and be best positioned of all when the race quickens.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts in a row before a below-par fifth last time, leaving him a fair each-way type on a rating of 63 (fifth of 11). Has raced over today's trip and going before, with a placed effort four back too.

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Has headgear (tongue-tie/blinkers) and races genuinely from off the pace, though shown in midfield here only because the hold-up ranks are oversubscribed; 0W1P in similar going and moderate recent form (8-4805) make him a tough proposition to support with confidence.
runners_data.comment: A rating of 70 (top of 11) marks him the most talented in the race on figures, back here after a 16-day break. The catch is a moderate recent sequence - yet to win in five starts without a top-three finish in that run.

runners_data.name: Ribston Pippin
runners_data.note: 59 days since last run is a flag, but the prominent style and record of winning on standard and artificial surfaces gives him course-relevant credentials; the trainer's 2/5 T14 return suggests the yard is in form and Sam James is a reliable pilot.
runners_data.comment: A below-par ninth last time out is the concern, though that follows a good second two starts back and a win four starts back. A rating of 60 (seventh of 11) makes him a fair, unproven type, and 59 days off adds another query.

runners_data.name: Electric Lightning
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer placed in this going-profile in a listed outing (2nd, 8f, Good), but recent form is flat (48-002) and the redistribution from rear to midfield captures the awkward reality that she will need significant gaps to appear from a genuinely back position in a competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, with two unplaced efforts among the recent form, though a good second last time out is a definite plus. A rating of 57 (ninth of 11) leaves plenty to find, though he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Oscar's Sister
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho-trained consistent placer who wears headgear and truly wants to come from off the pace — last five all in arrears — but 0W in 11 runs on similar going and the congested hold-up group makes a winning run mechanistically difficult however the race is run.
runners_data.comment: A below-par eighth last time continues a stop-start sequence, though a runner-up effort five back and a speed figure of 68 hint at more ability than the finishes suggest. A rating of 60 (eighth of 11) looks fair, and she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner (OR=48) but races prominently, carries a light 123lbs and has placed form over this trip on Tapeta; blinkered, recent run 11 days ago keeps her fit, and if the race produces a messy middle section her positional speed could catch the field cold.
runners_data.comment: On a rating of 55 (11th of 11) and an official mark of 48, he's up against it on figures, with the form cooling since a win five back. Quick back inside a fortnight, and has raced over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Relevant Range is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested position from the outset on this flat Doncaster mile, setting a sustainable gallop on ground riding Good To Firm throughout the card. That tempo — honest but not pressured — will likely produce a race where position off the pace matters enormously, with the prominent types Woodleigh and Ribston Pippin sitting ideally just behind the leader and able to respond without burning reserves. The prominent-to-midfield profile is clearly favoured here: horses who can track the pace within two or three lengths, avoid the scrimmage of a congested hold-up group, and produce a controlled late effort should hold a decisive positional edge. Note that the field contains more genuine hold-up types than can all settle at the rear on a one-mile flat track — Clasina, Give Me The Night, Electric Lightning, and Oscar's Sister are true come-from-behind horses shuffled into the midfield representation, but in practice they will be queuing behind each other in the closing stages with limited room to manoeuvre, meaning the race is most likely to be decided among horses racing in the front half.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Relevant Range Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Relevant Range dictates an uncontested, honest pace and the race is decided by those tracking closest.
scenarios.body: Woodleigh and Ribston Pippin sit within two lengths of the leader through the straight, benefiting from a predictable tempo that rewards rhythm and a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong; both have recent course-relevant form at this trip and on similar ground and are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so undemanding that Relevant Range steals an unassailable advantage and holds on as closers fail to close.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to pressure the leader early, Relevant Range bowls along in a near-solo breakaway and the hold-up horses burn through too much ground trying to get to her; Elle-May Croot dictates every yard and the prominent types who attempt a challenge simply find the winner already gone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Weave Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the hold-up brigade find gaps to deliver late runs.
scenarios.body: A slightly-quickened middle section compresses the field and creates late scrimmage, through which Penny Ghent or Palmarian — the most straightforwardly genuine rear-rankers — can find daylight in the final two furlongs; both have placed form at this distance and on good ground and represent the hold-up horses most likely to actually secure clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Midfield, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent and redistributed midfield horses interfere with each other leaving a gap for an unfancied runner.
scenarios.body: A bunched, scrappy middle portion of the race disrupts the rhythm of the fancied hold-up types who cannot find clear daylight, and First Encounter — racing from a prominent, competitive draw — benefits from a clean passage at a low weight; Princess Niyla's consistency at the trip also gives her an outside claim if the race sets up with late gaps.

watchPoints.text: Woodleigh sits in the golden spot on this pace map — tracking Relevant Range from a prominent pitch — and Kevin Stott's booking is significant; watch whether he moves to challenge turning in rather than waiting.

Penny Ghent's 49-day absence and blinkered headgear combination need monitoring in the paddock — she has won fresh before but a dull coat or fractious behaviour would meaningfully reduce her hold-up chance.

Clasina, Give Me The Night, Electric Lightning and Oscar's Sister are all genuine hold-up horses and will be fighting for the same ground in the straight — watch the early stages for whether any of them concede position entirely and get buried in rear.

Relevant Range's Good To Firm record is sparse (3 runs, 0 wins, 1 place) — if she shows any sign of faltering in the final two furlongs rather than kicking clear, the prominent pair Woodleigh and Ribston Pippin are poised to swoop immediately.

First Encounter holds the lowest official rating by some margin but is fresh (11 days), carries bottom weight, and races prominently with blinkers — worth monitoring in running given how little she has to lose tactically.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer with a fine record at 16f on good ground (8 from 15 in similar going, 3 wins and 7 places), making a very quick return just 3 days after its last run which warrants monitoring, but the short turnaround for this trainer has been fine recently (2 wins from 14 days); natural prominent racer ideally positioned in this small field.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last two starts, with a win three back underlining fair improvement, and a rating of 80 (top of four) makes him the one to beat on figures. Quick back just three days on, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Pergamon
runners_data.note: Holds an impressive winning record at 16f on good ground (5 wins from 13 similar-going runs) and arrives fresh on 16 days rest with headgear (tongue-tie) applied, but its natural prominent style could not be mapped to its preferred position given the race shape, meaning it faces the race out of role and its chance must be tempered accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: A rating of 75 (third of four) keeps him well involved, and a solid third two starts back shows the ability is there. Yet to win in four starts, with two eighths in that run, consistency is the query, though he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Pyleates
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old stepping up sharply from 12-14f to 2m½f for the first time, with only 0 wins and 1 place from 6 similar-going runs; genuine hold-up racer who will be last early and needs either a collapse in the pace or a very strong stamina superiority to get competitive over this marathon trip.|
runners_data.comment: A good second last time out, sandwiched by a blip two back and a pair of thirds further behind, points to solid recent form on a rating of 73 (fourth of four). Yet to win in five starts, and that below-par seventh two starts back is the one query.

runners_data.name: Tabasko
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter whose prominence in a small field comes cheaply, though this three-year-old faces a significant step up from 10-12f to 2m½f which is an unproven stamina test; Ed Walker's yard is in decent form (6 wins from 33 in 14 days) but the distance question is the dominant factor in assessing how long Tabasko can sustain the lead.|
runners_data.comment: A good second last time out continues a string of respectable efforts, and a rating of 77 (second of four) makes her a leading threat on figures. Yet to win in five starts, but the finishes suggest she's not far away.

races.paceDynamic: Tabasko is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four over 2m½f at Doncaster, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset with no meaningful pressure likely to force an early burn. An Bradan Feasa and Pergamon are both natural prominent types, but only one can realistically sit on Tabasko's shoulder — An Bradan Feasa, with his consistent record of racing in that position over this trip and going, is better placed to occupy it, while Pergamon is redistributed to a midfield mapping that does not reflect its true racing style, as the field carries more prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate. Pyleates is the sole genuine hold-up horse and will be last of four, tasked with picking up the pieces if the front end slows. With a controlled pace across a flat course and no rival likely to fire Tabasko into a truly hard early gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent racers with proven stamina on this ground are best positioned.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tabasko Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tabasko dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race develops into a sustained staying test from two out.
scenarios.body: Tabasko sets the fractions on his own terms and the runner-up spot is likely filled by An Bradan Feasa, who tracks throughout and has the form on this trip and going to mount a strong late challenge; the controlled pace rewards horses who travel comfortably in the first two positions without burning energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tabasko's gallop is so sedate that a blanket finish develops and Pyleates can produce a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: A funereal early tempo compresses the field, removing Tabasko's advantage and giving Pyleates — the only genuine hold-up type — the platform to produce a finishing effort that catches the leaders napping; however Pyleates' limited similar-going form and step up in trip make this the least reliable of the closers' routes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pergamon Rebounds From Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If Pergamon manages to recover its natural prominent position early and reproduces its strong winning form at this trip on good ground.
scenarios.body: Pergamon's five wins in its history have come prominently and it has winning form specifically at 16f on good, suggesting it can be potent when racing in its preferred role; however, being mapped out of position means it faces an early tactical battle to get comfortable, and the style-fit discount must be respected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Tabasko builds an unassailable lead in the final half-mile and the prominent horses cannot reel it in.
scenarios.body: Tabasko, stepping up markedly in trip from its recent 10-12f runs, surprises rivals by finding reserves late on a flat track and wins going away; this scenario depends on Tabasko handling the distance step-up better than its profile suggests, which is the key risk.

watchPoints.text: Tabasko's stamina over 2m½f is completely untested — if it ties up in the final furlong after leading throughout, An Bradan Feasa is best placed to capitalise having raced this trip repeatedly.

An Bradan Feasa runs just 3 days after its last outing; watch the market to see if connections are confident the horse has fully recovered before treating it as the main beneficiary of this pace shape.

Pergamon will need to battle for position early to override its redistributed mapping — watch the first two furlongs to see if it can get closer to the pace than the race shape suggests; if it does, its good-ground winning form over this trip becomes relevant.

With only four runners over a gruelling 2m½f trip, the race is likely to be run in a very tight pack early; any horse that becomes fractious in the preliminaries or is slow away will lose significant ground that is hard to recover at this distance.

Pyleates has consistently raced over shorter trips (12-14f) in recent form; monitor whether its jockey Lewis Edmunds attempts to take it closer to the pace than its hold-up profile suggests, which could indicate the stable believes the trip is within its range.
